learn.hook: Chew a bite of roti for a long time and it starts tasting a little sweet. Your saliva is already doing chemistry!
points: Digestion breaks food down into simple substances that the body can absorb and use.
The path of food: mouth → food pipe (oesophagus) → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → rectum → anus.
In the mouth, teeth break food into small pieces and saliva starts turning starch into sugar. Incisors cut, canines tear, and premolars and molars grind.

The stomach makes acid and digestive juices; the liver makes bile; the pancreas sends juices to the small intestine, where digestion is completed. Finger-like villi in the small intestine absorb the digested food into the blood.

The large intestine absorbs water and some salts from the undigested food. The waste leaves through the anus. Cows and buffaloes (ruminants) swallow grass quickly and later bring it back to chew as cud.

example.q: Why does a roti taste sweet if you chew it slowly for a minute?
steps: Saliva contains a substance that breaks starch down into sugar.
Sugar tastes sweet, so the roti starts tasting sweet.
example.answer: Saliva changes some of the starch in the roti into sugar.

learn.reallife: Doctors tell us to chew food well and eat fibre-rich food like fruits, vegetables and whole grains, so the digestive system works smoothly.

quiz.q: Where does the digestion of food begin?
quiz.explain: Teeth break food and saliva starts digesting starch right in the mouth.
quiz.mistake: Thinks digestion starts only in the stomach

quiz.q: Where is the digestion of food completed?
quiz.explain: Juices from the liver, pancreas and the intestine's own walls complete digestion in the small intestine.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the stomach finishes all digestion

quiz.q: What is the main job of the villi?
options: To absorb digested food into the blood
quiz.explain: Villi are tiny finger-like bumps that give a large surface for absorbing digested food.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what villi do

quiz.q: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
quiz.explain: The liver is the largest gland. It makes bile, which helps digest fats.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the stomach is a gland

quiz.q: Which pointed teeth are mainly used for tearing food?
quiz.explain: Canines are pointed teeth for tearing. Incisors cut and molars grind.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the jobs of different teeth

quiz.q: How many permanent teeth does an adult usually have?
quiz.explain: An adult usually has 32 permanent teeth. Children have 20 milk teeth.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up milk teeth (20) with permanent teeth

quiz.q: What does the large intestine mainly absorb?
quiz.explain: Most digested food is absorbed in the small intestine. The large intestine takes back water and some salts.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the large intestine absorbs most of the food

quiz.q: A cow is seen chewing even when she is not eating fresh grass. Why?
options: She is chewing cud, food brought back from her rumen
quiz.explain: Ruminants like cows store swallowed grass in the rumen and later bring it back to the mouth to chew properly.
quiz.mistake: Does not know about ruminants

teach.ask: Gappu ate a big plate of poha. Where does the food go after Gappu swallows it, and what happens on the way?
teach.praise: Chirp! From mouth to stomach to small intestine, the food is broken down and absorbed. Gappu's poha is now energy!
teach.nudge: Where does the digested food get absorbed into the blood?

learn.hook: Run up the stairs and you start huffing and puffing. Why does your body suddenly want so much more air?
points: Breathing means taking in air (inhaling) and giving out air (exhaling) through the nose and lungs.
Respiration is the process in the cells where food (glucose) is broken down using oxygen to release energy. Carbon dioxide and water are formed.
When we inhale, the diaphragm (a sheet of muscle below the lungs) moves down and the chest expands. When we exhale, it moves up and the chest becomes smaller.
During hard exercise, muscles may not get enough oxygen. Then they break down glucose without oxygen and form lactic acid, which can cause cramps.
Other animals breathe differently: fish use gills, earthworms breathe through their moist skin, insects have tiny holes called spiracles, and frogs use lungs and their moist skin.

example.q: Air you breathe out is bubbled through lime water using a straw, and it turns milky faster than when fresh air is pumped through. What does this show?
steps: Lime water turns milky with carbon dioxide.
Breathed-out air makes it milky faster.
So breathed-out air has more carbon dioxide.
example.answer: Exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide than the air we breathe in.

learn.reallife: Yoga breathing (pranayama) helps people breathe slowly and deeply. Athletes train to help their bodies use oxygen better.

games.title: Match the animal to how it breathes
Breathing check
items: Breathing and respiration mean exactly the same thing.
Breathing is taking air in and out; respiration is releasing energy from food inside cells.
The air we breathe out contains more carbon dioxide than the air we breathe in.
Our cells make carbon dioxide during respiration, and we breathe it out.
When we inhale, the diaphragm moves down.
This makes more space in the chest so air rushes into the lungs.
Muscles need more energy, so the body needs more oxygen.
Earthworms have no lungs; they breathe through their moist skin.

quiz.q: What is released during respiration in our cells?
quiz.explain: Glucose is broken down using oxygen to release energy, along with carbon dioxide and water.
quiz.mistake: Thinks respiration only means breathing air

quiz.q: Which gas do we need to take in for respiration?
quiz.explain: Cells use oxygen to break down glucose and release energy.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the gas taken in with the gas given out

quiz.q: What happens to the diaphragm when we breathe in?
quiz.explain: The diaphragm moves down and the ribs move up and out, so the chest becomes bigger and air flows in.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the movements of inhaling and exhaling

quiz.q: Why do muscles sometimes get cramps after hard exercise?
options: Lactic acid builds up when muscles get too little oxygen
quiz.explain: Without enough oxygen, muscles break glucose down without oxygen and form lactic acid, which causes cramps.
quiz.mistake: Does not know about respiration without oxygen in muscles

quiz.q: How does a fish breathe in water?
options: Using lungs at the surface every second
Using gills, which take oxygen dissolved in water
quiz.explain: Gills take in oxygen that is dissolved in the water.
quiz.mistake: Thinks fish do not need oxygen or breathe like humans

quiz.q: Which animal breathes through its moist skin?
quiz.explain: Earthworms have no lungs; gases pass through their moist skin.
quiz.mistake: Assumes all animals have lungs

quiz.q: Why is breathing through the nose better than breathing through the mouth?
options: Hairs and mucus in the nose trap dust and germs
The nose cools the lungs to ice
quiz.explain: The nose cleans the air before it reaches the lungs.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the nose filters air

quiz.q: Dolphins live in water but come up to the surface often. Why?
options: They have gills that need air
quiz.explain: Dolphins are mammals with lungs, so they must come up to breathe air through a blowhole.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every animal that lives in water uses gills

teach.ask: Gappu is panting after a long flight! What is the difference between breathing and respiration, and why does Gappu need oxygen?
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! Breathing brings in oxygen; respiration uses it to release energy from food. Gappu is ready to fly again!
teach.nudge: What does the body get when food is broken down using oxygen?

learn.hook: Your heart is about the size of your fist, yet it beats again and again every minute of your life without taking a holiday!
points: Blood carries oxygen, digested food and other useful things to every part of the body, and takes away wastes like carbon dioxide.
The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood. The human heart has four chambers.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins bring blood back to the heart. Tiny tubes called capillaries connect them.
Blood has red blood cells (carry oxygen; their red pigment is haemoglobin), white blood cells (fight germs) and platelets (help blood clot), floating in a liquid called plasma.
Each heartbeat sends a push of blood through the arteries. We can feel this as the pulse at the wrist or neck. Doctors listen to the heart with a stethoscope.

example.q: Ali counts his pulse while sitting, then again after skipping for two minutes. The second count is higher. Why?
steps: Skipping makes the muscles work harder.
Working muscles need more oxygen and food.
The heart beats faster to deliver blood more quickly, so the pulse rises.
example.answer: His heart beats faster after exercise to send more oxygen-rich blood to his muscles.

learn.reallife: Blood donation camps in India collect blood that can save lives in hospitals. Healthy adults can donate blood safely.

games.title: Match the part to its job
pairs: Carry blood away from the heart
Carry blood back to the heart

items.text: The red pigment in blood is ___.
Doctors use a ___ to hear the heartbeat.
The throbbing of arteries felt at the wrist is called the ___.

quiz.q: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
quiz.explain: The heart is a strong muscle that pumps blood through blood vessels.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the jobs of organs

quiz.q: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
quiz.explain: Arteries take blood away from the heart; veins bring it back.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up arteries and veins

quiz.q: What is the job of white blood cells?
quiz.explain: White blood cells protect the body by attacking germs.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up white and red blood cells

quiz.q: What gives blood its red colour?
quiz.explain: Haemoglobin is a red substance that also carries oxygen.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the name of the red pigment

quiz.q: When you get a small cut, the bleeding soon stops. Which part of blood helps?
quiz.explain: Platelets help form a clot that seals the cut.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what platelets do

quiz.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
quiz.explain: The human heart has four chambers: two on top and two below.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a smaller number

quiz.q: Why does your pulse rate go up after running?
options: The heart stops for a while
The heart beats faster to supply more oxygen
quiz.explain: Muscles need more oxygen during exercise, so the heart pumps faster.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect heart rate with the body's needs

quiz.q: What are the tiny blood vessels that connect arteries and veins called?
quiz.explain: Capillaries are very thin vessels where oxygen and food pass from blood to the body's cells.
quiz.mistake: Confuses capillaries with villi in the intestine

teach.ask: Gappu put a claw on its chest and felt thump-thump! What is the heart doing, and where does the blood go?
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! The heart pumps blood through arteries and veins to deliver oxygen and food everywhere. Thump-thump, Gappu!
teach.nudge: What does blood carry to all parts of the body?
